steps.text: Follow the path down out of the Great Deku Tree's meadow into Kokiri Forest village; Mido stops you at the bottom.
steps.detail: The scene plays by itself: Mido decides you killed the Great Deku Tree and storms off before you can answer. Nothing in the village has changed and no house or shop has anything you need.

steps.text: Cross the village to the log tunnel on the west side, the one straight opposite the path you just came down.
steps.detail: It is the tunnel at ground level past the small bridges, not the Lost Woods tunnel up on the ledge behind the Know-It-All Brothers' house. Saria is not at her usual spot on the bridge railing; she is waiting further on.

steps.text: Walk through the log tunnel onto the long bridge that leaves the forest.
Keep walking along the bridge until Saria drops down in front of you and the goodbye scene starts.
steps.detail: You cannot avoid her and there is nothing to answer. Kokiri are not supposed to leave the forest, which is why she came to see you off.

steps.text: Accept the Fairy Ocarina from Saria at the end of the scene.
steps.detail: It is her parting gift and the instrument you will play every song on until you get the Ocarina of Time. Link runs off on his own once the scene finishes.

steps.text: Open the pause menu and put the Fairy Ocarina on a C button.
steps.detail: Item subscreen: highlight the ocarina, then press the C button you want it on. You have no songs yet, so playing it now only makes noise.

steps.text: Step off the end of the bridge into Hyrule Field and watch the flyover of the field.
steps.detail: The camera sweeps the whole field and settles on Hyrule Castle in the distance to the north. That castle is where this chapter is going.

steps.text: Walk forward and round the first corner of the path; Kaepora Gaebora, a huge owl, lands on the tree ahead of you.
steps.detail: You cannot walk past him. He is a recurring guide and will drop in like this several more times during the game.

steps.text: Talk through the owl's speech about Hyrule Castle and about the map you now carry.
steps.detail: The content is just a reminder that the castle to the north is your destination and that the map works out here in the field too.

steps.text: Answer his closing question with the option that does not send him back to the start of the speech.
steps.detail: He asks whether you want to hear it all again. The 'no' answer is usually the bottom line, but the game shuffles the order of the two options between encounters, so read both before pressing A.

steps.text: Run straight north up the road toward the castle and do not stop to explore; going directly gets you to the drawbridge before nightfall.
steps.detail: Lon Lon Ranch, Kakariko Village, Lake Hylia, Gerudo Valley and the Lost Woods are all reachable already, but their story objectives are still locked. Their Heart Pieces and Gold Skulltulas are collected in later chapters, so leave them.

steps.text: Pass the walled Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of the field and stay on the road to the moat at the north edge.
steps.detail: The ranch is the fenced circle with a ramp gate. Keep it to one side and keep running; the road curves up to the castle moat and the drawbridge.

steps.text: If the drawbridge is already raised for the night, stand on the road and wait there for sunrise.
steps.detail: Stalchildren claw their way out of the ground at night, but only if you step off the road onto the grass. Standing still on the road is safe, and the bridge lowers again at dawn.

steps.text: Cross the drawbridge and go up the entry passage into Hyrule Castle Town.
Come up the passage into the Market entrance, the small courtyard just inside the town gate.
Go through the first door on your right in this entrance courtyard, into the guardhouse.
steps.detail: The soldier inside is on duty to stop people wrecking the storeroom, but he is bored and lets you smash the lot.

steps.text: Smash the pots and the loose crates around the guardhouse with your sword and pick up the Rupees.
steps.detail: Roll into the crates or slash them; either breaks them. This is the best Rupee source you have access to right now.

steps.text: Break the crate in the back corner right beside the soldier; a Gold Skulltula jumps out of it.
steps.detail: It is one of the crates stacked behind him at the far end of the room, not the ones near the door.

steps.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula with one sword slash and pick up the token it drops.
steps.detail: It scuttles along the floor rather than clinging to a wall, so you can just walk up and hit it. Walk over the token to collect it.

steps.text: Step out of the guardhouse door and walk straight back in to respawn the pots and crates, then smash them again until you hold at least 20 Rupees.
steps.detail: Leaving and re-entering resets the room every time. You need 20 Rupees for the Shooting Gallery; a child's wallet caps at 99.

steps.text: Leave the guardhouse, go back down the entry passage and out onto the drawbridge.
steps.detail: You are heading for three hidden Red Rupees on the bridge itself.

steps.text: Climb the chain on the left-hand side of the drawbridge all the way to the top.
steps.detail: Walk into the chain and Link grabs on, then climb with the stick. Go slowly; letting go drops you back to the bridge deck.

steps.text: From the top of that chain, jump off toward the middle of the bridge to grab a hidden Red Rupee worth 20.
steps.detail: Aim inward, over the bridge deck, not out toward the water. The Rupee is invisible until you touch it.

steps.text: Climb the chain on the other side of the drawbridge to the top the same way.
Jump toward the middle from that chain for the second hidden Red Rupee, 40 Rupees in total.
steps.detail: That is already more than the 20 the Shooting Gallery costs.

steps.text: For the third hidden Red Rupee, stand a little back from the wall on the chain, roll, and jump off from there.
steps.detail: This one sits in the centre of the bridge and only the rolling jump reaches it. It is fiddly; drop it after a few tries, the other 40 Rupees are enough.

steps.text: Walk back across the drawbridge and up into the Market square, the round plaza with the fountain.
Find the Shooting Gallery around the plaza: it is the shopfront with a bullseye sign hanging above its door.
steps.detail: Walk the ring of doors around the fountain until you see the bullseye. The Bazaar, the Happy Mask Shop and the Bombchu alley are the other doors here.

steps.text: Talk to the big-lipped owner inside and pay 20 Rupees for a round.
steps.detail: He hands you a round straight away once you agree and pay.

steps.text: Shoot all ten Rupee targets in one round with the Fairy Slingshot for a perfect score.
steps.detail: The targets pop up in exactly the same pattern every game, so a failed round is practice. Lead the moving ones: Deku Seeds take a moment to reach them. If you only miss one or two he lets you play again free, so keep going until the round is perfect.

steps.text: Take the bigger Bullet Bag that the perfect round earns; it holds 40 Deku Seeds.
steps.detail: Only the very first perfect round gives the bag. Perfect rounds after that pay 50 Rupees instead, which is still a decent earner.

steps.text: Step back out of the Shooting Gallery into the Market square.
Leave the Market square by the road on the north side and follow it up out of town to the Hyrule Castle grounds.
steps.detail: It is the archway opposite the way you came in from the drawbridge. The road climbs past the Temple of Time turning and ends at the castle gate area.

steps.text: Walk forward onto the castle grounds path; Kaepora Gaebora drops in front of you a second time.
Talk through the owl's speech about how time passes.
steps.detail: The useful part: time stands still inside the town and inside houses, but keeps moving out here and in Hyrule Field. Whenever you need day or night to change, wait out here, never in the Market.

steps.text: Roll into the lone tree standing to the left of the path near the entrance; a Gold Skulltula falls out of it.
steps.detail: Press A while running to roll, and hit the trunk square on. Nothing happens if you only walk into it.

steps.text: Slash the Gold Skulltula that landed at the foot of the tree and take its token.
steps.detail: One hit kills it on the ground. Step over the token to pick it up.

steps.text: Walk back down the road into the Market square.
steps.detail: This trip is what moves Malon. The red-haired girl who was standing in the Market goes up to the castle grounds once you have been up there and come back. If she was already at the vines on your first visit, skip this and the next step.

steps.text: Turn around and take the road back up to the castle grounds.
Walk over to the ivy-covered cliff to the left of the first guarded gate; Malon is standing at the bottom of it.
Talk to Malon and hear her out about her father.
steps.detail: She is from Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of Hyrule Field. Her father Talon came up to the castle to deliver crates of Lon Lon Milk and never came home; she is sure he has fallen asleep somewhere inside.

steps.text: Take the Weird Egg she gives you so you can wake Talon when you find him.
Put the Weird Egg on a C button in the pause menu.
steps.detail: It hatches into a Cucco at the next dawn, and only while time is running, so it will not hatch while you stand in town.

steps.text: Climb the vines on the cliff next to Malon to the top.
steps.detail: The gate beside her is guarded and the guard will not let you through; the cliff is the way in.

steps.text: Walk along the top of the cliff away from the gate, to the far end of the ledge.
steps.detail: Do not head toward the guard. Getting caught anywhere on the grounds dumps you back at the entrance and you restart the sneak from these vines.

steps.text: Drop off the end of the ledge and land on the far side of the gate.
Turn to face the castle and read the guards: two patrol the bright road up to the right, one stands higher up on the left.
Climb the grass slope straight up the gap between that pair on the right and the single guard on the left.
steps.detail: A guard only notices what is in front of him, so the gap between two patrols is safe as long as you keep moving and do not cut across anyone's face.

steps.text: At the top of the slope, get off the bright gravel road and stay on the grass to the left.
steps.detail: The road is where the patrols walk. The grass strip to its left runs parallel and is out of their view.

steps.text: Follow the grass forward on the left until a second gate with a guard on each side comes into view.
Go to the stones that stick out of the cliff face just to the left of that gate.
steps.detail: On the N64 version they are pale stones jutting from the rock; other versions draw vines there instead. Either way, walk into them and Link grabs on.

steps.text: Climb the stones to the top of the cliff.
Walk over the top and drop down on the other side of the gate, behind the two guards.
Ahead is a third gate with two more guards; instead of walking up to it, jump into the moat on the right.
steps.detail: There is no way past this gate on foot. The moat runs along the wall and around the guards.

steps.text: Swim along the moat, following the castle wall past the gate toward the far corner.
steps.detail: Link swims by himself once he is in; just steer. Watch the air meter and surface if it runs low, but the swim is short.

steps.text: Grab the Rupees floating in the moat as you swim past them.
steps.detail: They sit right along the route, so it costs nothing to pick them up on the way.

steps.text: Climb out of the moat at the far corner.
Follow the grass along the castle wall until you find Talon, fast asleep beside his crates of Lon Lon Milk.
If the Weird Egg has not hatched yet, stand here on the grounds and wait for dawn.
steps.detail: Time only moves outdoors, and here counts as outdoors, so waiting next to Talon works. The egg hatches into a Cucco at sunrise.

steps.text: Put the hatched Cucco on a C button in the pause menu.
Stand right next to Talon and use the Cucco; its crowing wakes him.
steps.detail: Get close enough that Link is almost touching him or the noise will not reach.

steps.text: Talk to Talon through his dialogue until he panics and runs off home.
steps.detail: He confirms Malon's story about the milk delivery and the nap, then bolts the moment he hears his daughter sent you after him. He leaves the crates behind, which is what you actually need.

steps.text: Grab the first milk crate with A and push it into the moat water against the wall.
steps.detail: Line yourself up square against a face of the crate before grabbing, then push it in. It floats and stays put.

steps.text: Push the second crate into the water so it snaps into place on top of the first.
steps.detail: It will only stack if you push it in beside the first one; the game clicks it into position.

steps.text: Climb onto the stack of crates.
Jump from the top crate across to the ledge where water pours out of the castle wall.
Check that it is daytime before you go any further; if night has fallen, drop back down and wait on the grounds for sunrise.
steps.detail: Two guards stand behind the hole at night and grab you the second you come through, throwing you back outside the grounds.

steps.text: Crawl through the small hole beside the waterspout into the castle courtyard.
Stand up out of the crawlspace and stay still for a moment to watch the first guard walk his loop.
steps.detail: The courtyard is a chain of small gardens, each with a guard walking a fixed circuit around the hedges, flower beds and statues. A guard sees only what is in front of him: behind him is safe, either side is not. Being spotted throws you all the way back outside the grounds, and you redo the whole sneak from Malon's vines.

steps.text: The moment the first guard turns away, walk up behind him and past along the hedge.
Slip past the next guard by keeping the flower bed between the two of you.
steps.detail: Move while he is on the far side of it, and stop when he swings back around toward your side.

steps.text: Move into the next stretch of the courtyard as soon as the guard there starts walking away from you.
Use the fountain in the middle of that stretch to stay out of the next guard's sight while he circles it.
steps.detail: Circle the fountain the same way he does, staying opposite him, until you are past.

steps.text: Cross behind the last guard and reach the far end of the courtyard.
steps.detail: This is the last one; after him nothing patrols.

steps.text: Turn left at the far end into the quiet part of the gardens.
steps.detail: No guards at all in here, so you can stop creeping.

steps.text: Shoot the window on the right-hand wall with the Fairy Slingshot for a Red Rupee.
steps.detail: The picture in that window is a cameo of Mario, Luigi, Yoshi, Peach and Bowser. Do not shoot the window on the left: a guard leans out of it and throws a Bomb at you.

steps.text: Walk up to Princess Zelda at the window at the back of the garden and talk to her.
steps.detail: She is peering through the glass into the throne room and does not notice you until you speak.

steps.text: Sit through her account of the Triforce and of the dream that foretold you.
steps.detail: Whoever touches the Triforce in the Sacred Realm is granted their wish, which is why the way in is sealed behind the three Spiritual Stones and the Ocarina of Time.

steps.text: Look through the window when she asks you to, and see Ganondorf kneeling before the King.
steps.detail: He notices you looking. This is the Gerudo man from her dream and the reason she is in a hurry.

steps.text: Agree to fetch the two remaining Spiritual Stones before Ganondorf can reach the Sacred Realm.
steps.detail: You already hold the Kokiri's Emerald from the Great Deku Tree; the Goron's Ruby and the Zora's Sapphire are still out there.

steps.text: Take Zelda's Letter from her at the end of the conversation.
steps.detail: It carries her royal seal and proves you act on her authority. You will need to show it to the guard blocking the Death Mountain gate in Kakariko Village.

steps.text: Walk back toward the garden exit; Impa, Zelda's attendant, steps in front of you.
Listen to Impa and let her teach you Zelda's Lullaby.
steps.detail: Notes: C-Left, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up, C-Right. Link plays it through by himself during the scene and it is added to your song list. It opens anything marked with the royal family's crest.

steps.text: Let Impa lead you out of the castle and point out Kakariko Village at the foot of Death Mountain.
steps.detail: The cutscene carries you all the way out and leaves you on the road outside Castle Town in Hyrule Field. Death Mountain is next in the story, but the following chapter clears several side areas first.
